text: Last reaction: chlorine substitutes hydrogen. In the dark, it is selective. Only the alpha hydrogens, on the carbons next to oxygen, are replaced, giving the alpha, alpha dichloro ether. In bright sunlight, every hydrogen goes: perchloro diethyl ether, with ten molecules of chlorine.
